news_article_ldjson.description: CNBC traders picked Zscaler, ServiceNow and Spotify; analyst targets supported the first two, while Spotify jumped 11.1% despite a Q3 earnings miss.
news_article_ldjson.headline: ServiceNow, Zscaler and a Music Streaming Giant on CNBC’s ‘Final Trades’ - ServiceNow (NYSE:NOW)
news_article_ldjson.articleBody: On CNBC’s "Halftime Report Final Trades," Malcolm Ethridge, managing partner at Capital Area Planning Group, picked Zscaler, Inc. (NASDAQ:ZS).    DA Davidson analyst Rudy Kessinger initiated coverage of Zscaler on Wednesday with a Neutral rating and a price target of $215.    Rob Sechan, CEO of NewEdge Wealth, named ServiceNow, Inc. (NYSE:NOW) as his final trade.    Supporting his choice, Truist Securities analyst Miller Jump on Wednesday maintained ServiceNow with a Buy rating and raised the price target from $130 to $180.    Don’t forget to check out our premarket coverage here     Joshua Brown, co-founder and CEO of Ritholtz Wealth Management, recommended Spotify Technology S.A. (NYSE:SPOT).    Spotify shares rose sharply on Thursday despite the music streaming company missing Wall Street estimates on third-quarter earnings and revenue, as continued growth in premium subscribers and monthly active users lifted investor sentiment.    Spotify reported earnings of $2.85 per share, missing analysts’ consensus estimate of $3.11. Revenue rose 16% year over year to 4.97 billion euros ($5.72 billion), slightly below the consensus estimate of $5.73 billion.    Price Action:     Zscaler shares gained 2.8% to close at $237.76 on Thursday.    ServiceNow shares rose 2.5% to close at $157.00.    Spotify shares jumped 11.1% to settle at $583.66 on Thursday.
